description: A VRF of the router: a kernel VRF device of the document's name, its routing table and the links it holds. Other router kinds name it by its name; the default VRF, of every link no VRF holds, has no document.

conntrackZone.description: Conntrack zone of the connections through the VRF's links, which no other VRF uses; null shares zone 0 with the default VRF and every VRF without one. A zone keeps the state and NAT of the VRF's connections apart from those of other VRFs with the same addresses. A VRF with a zone neither imports routes from another VRF nor gives its routes to one.

interfaces.description: Links the VRF holds, by name or glob, a glob being a prefix followed by `*`; a glob stands for the links the node's Network documents name in a `[Match]` section's `Name=`. A link is named by a Network document, which gets `VRF=`, and every link of that Network is in this VRF.

table.description: Routing table of the VRF, which no other VRF uses; not 253, 254 or 255, the kernel's tables of the default VRF. A change creates the VRF anew, which ends the sessions in it.

title: VRF

rules.description: A VRF is named as its device, in 15 characters at most, and not default.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, n == "default" || size(n) > 15).map(n, "VRF " + n).join(", ") + ": a VRF is named as its device, in 15 characters at most, and default names the VRF of every link no VRF holds"

rules.description: A VRF's table is none of the kernel's own: 253, 254 and 255.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, documents[n].spec.table in [253, 254, 255]).map(n, "VRF " + n).join(", ") + " uses table 253, 254 or 255, which the kernel keeps for the default VRF; give it another number"

rules.description: A table belongs to one VRF.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(t, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.table), "more than one VRF uses table " + string(t.filter(x, size(t.filter(y, y == x)) > 1)[0]) + "; give each VRF a table of its own")
rules.rule: cel.bind(t, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.table), t.all(x, size(t.filter(y, y == x)) == 1))

rules.description: An interface or glob is in one VRF, once; globs compare as written.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(all, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.interfaces).flatten(), "the interface " + all.filter(i, size(all.filter(j, j == i)) > 1)[0] + " is in more than one VRF, or twice in one; give each interface one VRF")
rules.rule: cel.bind(all, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.interfaces).flatten(), all.all(i, size(all.filter(j, j == i)) == 1))
